questions.question: The reaction NaOH + HCl rightarrow NaCl + H₂O is an example of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Double displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Double displacement reaction** is a type of chemical process where two compounds react, and the **positive ions (cations)** and the **negative ions (anions)** of the two reactants switch places to form two new compounds.
 
• The reaction **NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O** involves **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, which is a strong base, and **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, which is a strong acid.
 
• In this reaction, the **Sodium (Na+)** ion from the base combines with the **Chloride (Cl-)** ion from the acid to form **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**. Simultaneously, the **Hydrogen (H+)** ion from the acid combines with the **Hydroxyl (OH-)** ion from the base to form **Water (H2O)**.
 
• This specific type of double displacement reaction is also widely known as a **Neutralization reaction**, as the acidic and basic properties are neutralized to produce a salt and water.
 
• The general formula for such a reaction is **AB + CD → AD + CB**, representing the exchange of partners between the reacting chemical species.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Decomposition reaction:**
 
 
• This is a reaction where a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products.
 
• An example is the heating of **Calcium Carbonate (CaCO3)**, which decomposes into **Calcium Oxide (CaO)** and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**.
 
• These reactions often require energy in the form of **heat, light, or electricity** to break the chemical bonds.
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction:**
 
 
• Also known as a **Single Displacement reaction**, it occurs when a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its salt solution.
 
• For example, when **Iron (Fe)** is placed in a **Copper Sulfate (CuSO4)** solution, it displaces copper to form **Iron Sulfate (FeSO4)**.
 
• This is governed by the **Reactivity Series** of metals.
 
 
 
• **Precipitation reaction:**
 
 
• This is a sub-category of double displacement reactions where two soluble salts react in an aqueous solution to produce an **insoluble solid** called a **precipitate**.
 
• While the reaction between **NaOH** and **HCl** is a double displacement, it is not a precipitation reaction because the resulting **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** remains soluble in water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **pH Level:** In a complete neutralization reaction between a strong acid and a strong base like **NaOH** and **HCl**, the resulting solution typically has a **pH of 7** at **25 degrees Celsius**, indicating a neutral state.
 
• **Exothermic Nature:** Most neutralization and double displacement reactions of this type are **exothermic**, meaning they release energy in the form of **heat** to the surroundings.
 
• **Applications:** Neutralization reactions are used in various fields, such as treating **indigestion** (using antacids to neutralize stomach acid), **wastewater treatment**, and adjusting **soil pH** in agriculture.
 
• **Ionic Form:** When written in net ionic form, the reaction is simply **H+ + OH- → H2O**, showing that the essential change is the formation of water from **Hydrogen** and **Hydroxyl** ions.

questions.question: In the reaction {MnO}₂ + 4{HCl} rightarrow {MnCl}₂ + 2{H}₂{O} + {Cl}₂ , which substance is oxidised and which substance is reduced?
questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**MnO2 is reduced, HCl is oxidised**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given chemical reaction is **MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2**. This reaction is a **Redox reaction** (Reduction-Oxidation), where both oxidation and reduction occur simultaneously.
 
• In **MnO2** (Manganese Dioxide), the **oxidation state** of **Manganese (Mn)** is **+4**. In the product **MnCl2** (Manganese Chloride), its oxidation state changes to **+2**. Since the oxidation number decreases, **MnO2 is reduced**.
 
• Alternatively, **reduction** is defined as the **removal of oxygen**. In this reaction, **MnO2** loses oxygen to form **MnCl2**. ***Hence, the statement that MnO2 is reduced is correct.***
 
• In **HCl** (Hydrochloric Acid), the **oxidation state** of **Chlorine (Cl)** is **-1**. In the product **Cl2** (Chlorine gas), which is in its elemental form, the oxidation state is **0**. Since the oxidation number increases, **HCl is oxidised**.
 
• Furthermore, **oxidation** is also defined as the **removal of hydrogen**. In this reaction, **HCl** loses hydrogen to form **Cl2**. ***Hence, the statement that HCl is oxidised is correct.***
 
• Therefore, **MnO2** acts as the **oxidizing agent** (it oxidizes HCl), and **HCl** acts as the **reducing agent** (it reduces MnO2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxidation and Reduction (Classical Concept):**
 
 
• **Oxidation** is the addition of **oxygen** or an electronegative element to a substance, or the removal of **hydrogen** or an electropositive element.
 
• **Reduction** is the removal of **oxygen** or an electronegative element from a substance, or the addition of **hydrogen** or an electropositive element.
 
 
 
• **Electronic Concept of Redox:**
 
 
• **Oxidation** involves the **loss of electrons** by an atom, ion, or molecule. This results in an increase in the **oxidation number**.
 
• **Reduction** involves the **gain of electrons**. This results in a decrease in the **oxidation number** of the substance.
 
 
 
• **Oxidizing and Reducing Agents:**
 
 
• An **Oxidizing Agent** (or oxidant) is a substance that accepts electrons and gets reduced. In the reaction, **MnO2** accepts electrons to go from **Mn(+4)** to **Mn(+2)**.
 
• A **Reducing Agent** (or reductant) is a substance that donates electrons and gets oxidised. In the reaction, **HCl** (specifically the Chloride ion) loses electrons to go from **Cl(-1)** to **Cl(0)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reaction Specifics:**
 
 
• This specific reaction is used in the **laboratory preparation of chlorine gas**. Concentrated **Hydrochloric acid** is reacted with **Manganese dioxide** to produce **Chlorine**, **Manganese(II) chloride**, and **Water**.
 
• The **oxidation state** of Oxygen remains **-2** throughout the reaction, and the oxidation state of Hydrogen remains **+1**, meaning they are not the primary species undergoing redox changes.
 
 
 
• **Common Redox Examples:**
 
 
• **Corrosion**: The **rusting of iron** is a redox reaction where iron is oxidised by atmospheric oxygen in the presence of moisture.
 
• **Combustion**: Burning of fuels like **methane (CH4)** in oxygen involves the oxidation of carbon and reduction of oxygen.
 
• **Photosynthesis**: This is a complex biological redox process where **Carbon dioxide** is reduced to glucose and **Water** is oxidised to oxygen.

questions.question: Burrs with hooks or spines are commonly dispersed by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Animals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The dispersal of seeds and fruits is a biological necessity to prevent overcrowding and ensure that new plants grow in diverse locations. Burrs are specific types of seeds or dry fruits equipped with **hooks, spines, or teeth**.
 
• These specialized appendages allow the seeds to easily **attach to the fur or skin of animals** or the **clothing of humans** as they pass by the plant.
 
• This method of dispersal is scientifically known as **Epizoochory**, where the seed is carried on the outside of an animal. This is a highly effective way for the plant to transport its offspring across **long distances**.
 
• Common examples of plants that use this mechanism include **Xanthium (Cocklebur)**, **Urena**, and **Burdock**. These plants produce fruits that are sticky or prickly to ensure they do not fall directly under the parent plant.
 
• By hitching a ride on mobile organisms, these plants can colonize **new habitats** and reduce competition for **sunlight, water, and soil nutrients**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dispersal by Air (Anemochory):**
 
 
• Plants like **Dandelion**, **Maple**, and **Drumstick** have seeds with **wings or hair**.
 
• These **lightweight** structures act like **parachutes**, allowing the **wind** to carry them over vast areas.
 
 
 
• **Dispersal by Water (Hydrochory):**
 
 
• Aquatic or semi-aquatic plants, such as **Coconut** and **Lotus**, develop seeds with a **fibrous or spongy outer coat**.
 
• This adaptation provides **buoyancy**, enabling the seeds to **float** and travel via **rivers or ocean currents** to distant shores.
 
 
 
• **Dispersal by Explosion (Autochory):**
 
 
• Some plants, like **Balsam**, **Pea**, and **Castor**, use mechanical energy.
 
• The fruit or **pod bursts open with a sudden jerk** when it dries, scattering the seeds in multiple directions away from the **parent plant**.
 
 
 
• **Dispersal by Gravity (Barochory):**
 
 
• Heavy fruits, such as **Apples** or **Oak acorns**, simply drop to the ground. While some may roll away, most stay near the **base of the tree** unless moved by secondary agents.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Velcro Inspiration:** The invention of **Velcro** in **1941** by **Swiss engineer George de Mestral** was inspired by observing how **Burdock burrs** stuck to his dog’s fur. This is a classic example of **biomimicry**.
 
• **Seed Longevity:** Seeds dispersed by animals often have a **hard protective coat** to prevent damage during the transport process or while being **excreted** (if they are eaten, known as **Endozoochory**).
 
• **Ecological Impact:** Seed dispersal plays a **vital role** in maintaining **biodiversity** and helping forests recover after natural disasters like **forest fires** or **landslides**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following best describes mechanical energy?

options.text: The sum of light energy and chemical energy
Energy stored in food and fuel
The sum of potential energy and kinetic energy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The sum of potential energy and kinetic energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mechanical energy** is defined as the energy possessed by an object due to its **motion** or its **position**. It represents the capacity of a physical system to perform **work**.
 
• It is the **sum of kinetic energy and potential energy** in a system. The mathematical formula is **M.E. = K.E. + P.E.**.
 
• **Kinetic energy** is the energy of an object resulting from its **motion**. Any object that has mass and is moving possesses this form of energy. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Potential energy** is the **stored energy** an object has because of its position relative to other objects, stresses within itself, or its electric charge. Common examples include a stretched **spring** or an object held at a certain **height**.
 
• The principle of **mechanical energy** is central to classical mechanics, where it is often conserved in a system that is subject only to **conservative forces**, such as gravity or ideal elastic forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE):**
 
 
• The **kinetic energy** of an object is given by the formula **1/2 mv²**, where **m** is the **mass** of the object and **v** is its **velocity**.
 
• If the velocity of an object is **doubled**, its kinetic energy increases **four times** because the energy is proportional to the square of the speed.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy (PE):**
 
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy** is calculated using the formula **mgh**, where **m** is the mass, **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth), and **h** is the **height** above a reference point.
 
• **Elastic Potential Energy** is stored when a material is deformed, such as in a compressed **gas** or a stretched **bowstring**.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Mechanical Energy:**
 
 
• In an isolated system where only **conservative forces** act, the **Total Mechanical Energy** remains constant over **time**.
 
• For example, in a **simple pendulum**, at the highest point (peak of the swing), the energy is entirely **potential**. At the lowest point (center of the swing), the energy is entirely **kinetic**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Energies:**
 
 
• **Chemical Energy:** This is energy stored in the **bonds** of chemical compounds (like **food** and **fuel**). It is released during a chemical reaction. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect*** as it describes chemical energy, not mechanical.
 
• **Solar Energy:** This is **radiant light** and heat from the **Sun** that is harnessed using technologies like **photovoltaics**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **SI unit** of mechanical energy is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **one Newton-meter**.
 
• Mechanical energy can be converted into other forms, such as **electrical energy** in a hydroelectric dam or **thermal energy** due to **friction**.
 
• In the presence of **non-conservative forces** like **air resistance** or **friction**, mechanical energy is not conserved but is instead transformed into **heat**.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**milch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **cattle farming**, animals are categorized based on their primary utility. **Milk-producing animals**, including cows, buffaloes, goats, and camels, are professionally termed **milch animals**.
 
• The production of milk is largely dependent on the **lactation period**, which is the duration of milk production after the birth of a calf. Milch animals are bred and managed to optimize this period.
 
• **Buffaloes** (*Bubalus bubalis*) are significant milch animals in **India**, contributing a major portion of the total milk production due to the high fat content in their milk. ***Hence, the correct option is milch.***
 
• Common high-yielding milch breeds of buffalo in India include **Murrah**, **Mehsana**, and **Surti**. These breeds are known for their efficiency in converting feed into high-quality milk.
 
• The management of these animals involves proper **shelter**, **balanced nutrition** (roughage and concentrates), and regular **veterinary check-ups** to ensure disease-free production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• They belong to the categories of **crustaceans** or **mollusks** and are not related to cattle farming. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• In **poultry farming**, **layers** are birds specifically raised for **egg production**.
 
• They start laying eggs at the age of about **20 weeks**. Common examples include **Leghorns**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Broilers**:
 
 
• **Broilers** are poultry birds raised specifically for **meat production**.
 
• They are bred for fast growth and high feed-conversion ratios, typically reaching market weight within **6 to 8 weeks**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Draught Animals**:
 
 
• Apart from milch animals, cattle used for **agricultural labor** such as **tilling**, **irrigation**, and **carting** are called **draught animals**. Bullocks are the most common example in this category.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **White Revolution**: Also known as **Operation Flood**, it was launched in **1970** to make India a self-dependent nation in milk production. **Dr. Verghese Kurien** is known as the **Father of the White Revolution** in India.
 
• **Nutritional Requirements**: Milch animals require a diet rich in **fiber** (roughage) for digestion and **concentrates** (proteins and minerals) for high milk yield.
 
• **Disease Management**: Cattle are prone to diseases like **Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD)** and **Anthrax**, which can drastically reduce milk production and require timely **vaccination**.
 
• **India's Global Standing**: **India** is the **largest producer of milk** in the world, contributing significantly to the global dairy market, with buffaloes playing a more dominant role than cows in the Indian context.
</ul

questions.question: Movement of gases such as {CO}₂ or {O}₂ across the cell membrane occurs by __________, from ________ concentration to ________ concentration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**diffusion; high; low**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The movement of gases like **Oxygen (O2)** and **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)** across the **cell membrane** takes place through a physical process known as **diffusion**.
 
• **Diffusion** is defined as the spontaneous movement of a substance from a region of **high concentration** to a region of **low concentration** until an equilibrium is reached.
 
• In biological systems, **CO2** (a cellular waste) accumulates in **high concentrations** inside the cell. Since the external environment has a **lower concentration** of **CO2**, the gas moves **out of the cell**.
 
• Conversely, when the concentration of **O2** inside the cell decreases due to **metabolic activities**, **O2** from the external environment (where it is at a **high concentration**) enters the cell by **diffusion**.
 
• This process is a form of **passive transport**, meaning it does not require any **metabolic energy (ATP)** to move the molecules across the **lipid bilayer** of the membrane. ***Hence, the correct option is diffusion; high; low.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Active Transport**:
 
 
• Unlike **diffusion**, **active transport** moves molecules or ions **against a concentration gradient** (from **low to high** concentration).
 
• This process requires **cellular energy**, usually in the form of **Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP)**, and often involves specific **membrane proteins** acting as pumps, such as the **Sodium-Potassium pump**.
 
 
 
• **Osmosis**:
 
 
• **Osmosis** is a specific type of **diffusion** involving the movement of **water molecules** through a **selectively permeable membrane**.
 
• Water moves from a region of **high water concentration** (dilute solution) to a region of **low water concentration** (concentrated solution).
 
 
 
• **Endocytosis**:
 
 
• **Endocytosis** is a **bulk transport** mechanism where the **plasma membrane** engulfs external food particles or substances to form a **vesicle** inside the cell.
 
• An example is **Amoeba**, which acquires its food through **endocytosis** (specifically **phagocytosis**) due to the **flexibility** of its cell membrane.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cell Membrane Permeability**: The **plasma membrane** is **selectively permeable**, allowing only certain substances like small **non-polar molecules** (**O2**, **CO2**, and **N2**) to pass through easily via **simple diffusion**.
 
• **Factors Affecting Diffusion**: The rate of **gas exchange** is influenced by the **concentration gradient**, the **permeability** of the membrane, **temperature**, and the **surface area** available for exchange.

questions.question: The type of pollination where pollen grains are transferred from one flower to another of the same species through wind is called _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**anemophily**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anemophily** is a form of **abiotic pollination** where **wind** is the primary agent used to transfer pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower.
 
• Plants that rely on **anemophily** do not need to attract pollinators like insects or birds; therefore, their flowers are typically **small**, **inconspicuous**, and **colorless**.
 
• These flowers generally lack **nectar** and **fragrance** because these features are energetically expensive and unnecessary for wind-based dispersal.
 
• The **pollen grains** produced by anemophilous plants are **lightweight**, **dry**, and **non-sticky**, allowing them to be easily carried by even light breezes over long distances.
 
• To maximize the chances of pollination, these plants produce pollen in **massive quantities**. For instance, a single **Maize** plant can produce millions of pollen grains.
 
• The **stigma** of such plants is often **large and feathery** (plumose) to provide a greater surface area for catching drifting pollen grains from the air.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Entomophily**:
 
 
• This is pollination by **insects** such as **bees**, **butterflies**, and **moths**.
 
• Flowers are usually **brightly colored**, possess a **strong scent**, and provide **nectar** as a reward to the insect.
 
• The **pollen grains** are typically **sticky** or **spiny** so they can easily adhere to the body of the insect.
 
 
 
• **Hydrophily**:
 
 
• This refers to pollination mediated by **water**. This is quite rare, occurring in only about **30 genera** of mostly monocotyledonous aquatic plants.
 
• Examples include **Vallisneria** and **Hydrilla**. In these plants, pollen grains are often **long and ribbon-like** and are protected from wetting by a **mucilaginous covering**.
 
 
 
• **Ornithophily**:
 
 
• This is pollination carried out by **birds**, such as **hummingbirds** and **sunbirds**.
 
• **Ornithophilous** flowers are usually **large**, **sturdy**, and **tubular** to accommodate the bird's beak. They are often **bright red** or **orange** but usually lack a distinct scent as birds have a poor sense of smell.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Gymnosperms**: Almost all **Gymnosperms**, such as **Pinus**, are wind-pollinated. They often release so much pollen that it creates a phenomenon known as "**Sulphur showers**" in pine forests.
 
• **Location of Anthers**: In wind-pollinated flowers, the **anthers** are often **well-exposed** (versatile) so that the pollen can be easily dispersed into the wind currents.
 
• **Biological Classification**: Pollination is broadly divided into **Self-pollination** (Autogamy) and **Cross-pollination** (Allogamy). **Anemophily** is a major mechanism for **Cross-pollination** in the plant kingdom.

• The resulting material, known as **compost**, is highly rich in **organic matter** and essential **nutrients** like **Nitrogen**, **Phosphorus**, and **Potassium (NPK)**.

• **Fertilization**: 
 
 
• In a biological context, **fertilization** is the fusion of **male and female gametes** to form a **zygote**.
 
• In an agricultural context, it refers to the application of **chemical fertilizers** or **organic manures** to the soil to enhance **crop yield** by providing specific **nutrients**.
 
 
 
• **Green Manuring**: 
 
 
• This involves growing specific crops, usually **leguminous plants** like **Sunn hemp** or **Guar**, which are then ploughed back into the soil while still **green**.
 
• The **green plants** decompose and enrich the soil specifically with **Nitrogen** and **organic matter**, acting as a natural fertilizer.
 
 
 
• **Organic Matter**: 
 
 
• It consists of **carbon-based compounds** that have come from the remains of organisms such as **plants** and **animals** and their waste products in the environment.
 
• **Organic matter** is essential for maintaining **soil fertility** and supports a healthy **ecosystem** of soil microbes.

• **Environmental Impact**: By converting **farm waste** into **compost**, farmers can reduce **methane emissions** that would otherwise occur if the waste were left to rot in **landfills**.
 
• **Soil Health**: Regular application of **compost** increases the **Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC)** of the soil, which helps the soil retain **nutrients** more effectively.

questions.question: Which of the following hydrocarbons contains a branched chain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Isobutane**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Hydrocarbons** are organic compounds consisting entirely of **carbon** and **hydrogen**. Based on the arrangement of carbon atoms, they are categorized into straight-chain, **branched-chain**, or cyclic structures. 
• **Isobutane**, also known as **2-methylpropane**, is the simplest alkane containing a **branched chain**. It has the molecular formula **C4H10**. 
• In **Isobutane**, the **carbon skeleton** is not a continuous line; instead, it features a **central carbon** atom bonded to three other methyl groups. ***Hence, the correct answer is Isobutane.*** 
• **Butane** (or n-butane) is a **straight-chain hydrocarbon** where all **four carbon atoms** are linked in a continuous sequence without any branching. 
• **Methane** (**CH4**) contains only **one carbon atom**, and **Ethene** (**C2H4**) contains only **two carbon atoms**; neither can form a branched chain because branching requires a minimum of **four carbon atoms** in saturated hydrocarbons. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Structural Isomerism:** This is a phenomenon where molecules have the **same molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements**. **Butane** and **Isobutane** are **structural isomers** because both share the formula **C4H10** but differ in their connectivity. 
• **Physical Properties:** Branching significantly affects physical properties. For example, **Isobutane** has a **lower boiling point** (approximately **-11.7°C**) compared to **n-Butane** (**-0.5°C**) because the branched shape reduces the **surface area**, leading to weaker **Van der Waals forces**. 
• **IUPAC Nomenclature:** According to **IUPAC** rules, the longest chain in **Isobutane** is three carbons long (**propane**), with a **methyl group** (**-CH3**) attached to the **second carbon**, resulting in the name **2-methylpropane**. 
• **Industrial Uses:** **Isobutane** is commonly used as a **refrigerant** (known as **R-600a**) and as a **propellant** in aerosol cans due to its low environmental impact compared to **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**. 
• **Saturated vs. Unsaturated:** Alkanes like **butane** and **isobutane** are **saturated hydrocarbons** (only single bonds), whereas **Ethene** is an **unsaturated hydrocarbon** containing a **double bond** between carbon atoms. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The number of **isomers** increases as the number of **carbon atoms** in a hydrocarbon increases. While **Butane** has only **2 isomers**, **Pentane** (**C5H12**) has **3**, and **Decane** (**C10H22**) has **75** possible structural isomers. 
• **Tertiary Carbon:** **Isobutane** is notable for having a **tertiary carbon atom**, which is a carbon atom bonded to **three other carbon atoms**. This structural feature is a hallmark of branching. 
• **Octane Rating:** In the **petroleum industry**, branched-chain hydrocarbons are highly valued because they burn more smoothly in internal combustion engines, contributing to a **higher octane rating** compared to straight-chain hydrocarbons.

questions.question: The number of protons in an element with atomic number 10 is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• The **atomic number** (represented by the symbol **Z**) of a chemical element is defined as the **number of protons** found in the nucleus of every atom of that element. 

• Since the question states the **atomic number is 10**, the number of **protons** must also be **10**. This is a direct one-to-one relationship defined by the laws of chemistry. 

• The element with **atomic number 10** is **Neon (Ne)**, which is a member of the **noble gas** family. 

• In a **neutral atom**, the number of **protons** is always equal to the number of **electrons**. Therefore, a neutral atom of **Neon** possesses **10 protons** and **10 electrons**. 

• The identity of an element is determined solely by its **atomic number**; changing the number of **protons** would change the element itself. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Mass Number (A):** 
 

• The **mass number** is the sum of the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** in the nucleus of an atom. 

• For the most abundant isotope of **Neon**, the **mass number** is **20**, meaning it contains **10 protons** and **10 neutrons**. 
 
 

• **Subatomic Particles:** 
 

• **Proton:** Discovered by **Ernest Rutherford**, it carries a **positive charge** of **+1** unit and has a mass of approximately **1.672 x 10^-27 kg**. 

• **Electron:** Discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897**, it carries a **negative charge** of **-1** unit and orbits the nucleus. 

• **Neutron:** Discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**, it is **electrically neutral** and resides within the nucleus along with **protons**. 
 
 

• **Neon (Ne) Characteristics:** 
 

• **Neon** is located in **Group 18** (Noble Gases) and **Period 2** of the **Modern Periodic Table**. 

• It was discovered in **1898** by **Sir William Ramsay** and **Morris Travers** in **London**. 

• It is chemically **inert** because it has a full **valence shell** of **8 electrons** (electronic configuration **2, 8**). 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Atomic Number vs Atomic Mass:** 
 

• The **Modern Periodic Law**, proposed by **Henry Moseley** in **1913**, states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their **atomic numbers**, not their **atomic weights**. 

• This classification corrected anomalies in **Mendeleev's Periodic Table**. 
 
 

• **Isotopes and Ions:** 
 

• **Isotopes** are atoms of the same element that have the same **atomic number** (protons) but different **mass numbers** (neutrons). **Neon** has three stable isotopes: **Ne-20**, **Ne-21**, and **Ne-22**. 

• In **Ions**, the number of **electrons** changes (lost or gained), but the number of **protons** remains strictly constant to maintain the element's identity. 
 
 

• **Uses of Neon:** 
 

• It is widely used in **advertising signs** (neon lights), **high-voltage indicators**, **lightning arresters**, and **gas lasers**.

questions.question: A force of 10 N causes mass m₁ to accelerate at 20 m/s² and mass m₂ to accelerate at 40 m/s². What acceleration will the same force produce if both masses are tied together?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.3 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, the **force (F)** acting on an object is equal to the product of its **mass (m)** and its **acceleration (a)**, expressed by the formula **F = ma**.
 
• For the first mass **m₁**, the given force is **10 N** and the acceleration produced is **20 m/s²**. By rearranging the formula to **m = F/a**, we find that **m₁ = 10 / 20 = 0.5 kg**.
 
• For the second mass **m₂**, the same force of **10 N** produces an acceleration of **40 m/s²**. Using the formula, we find that **m₂ = 10 / 40 = 0.25 kg**.
 
• When both masses are **tied together**, they act as a single system with a combined mass **M**. Therefore, the total mass **M = m₁ + m₂ = 0.5 kg + 0.25 kg = 0.75 kg**.
 
• To find the new acceleration **a** produced by the same **10 N** force on the combined mass, we use **a = F / M**. Calculating this gives **a = 10 / 0.75 = 13.33 m/s²**. ***Hence, the resulting acceleration is approximately 13.3 m/s².***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion**: This fundamental law of **Classical Mechanics** states that the rate of change of **momentum** of a body is directly proportional to the applied **force** and takes place in the direction in which the force acts. It provides the quantitative definition of force.
 
• **Force (F)**: It is a **vector quantity** measured in **Newtons (N)**. One Newton is the amount of force required to accelerate a **1 kg** mass at a rate of **1 m/s²**.
 
• **Mass (m)**: Mass is a **scalar quantity** representing the amount of matter in an object and is a measure of its **inertia**. The **SI unit** for mass is the **kilogram (kg)**.
 
• **Acceleration (a)**: Acceleration is the rate at which an object changes its **velocity**. It is a vector quantity measured in **meters per second squared (m/s²)**. If the force remains **constant**, the acceleration is **inversely proportional** to the mass of the object.
 
• **Inertia**: This is the inherent property of an object to resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion. Greater mass implies **greater inertia**, meaning a larger force is required to achieve the same acceleration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Consistent Units**: When solving physics problems, it is crucial to ensure all units are in the **SI system** (Newtons, Kilograms, Meters, Seconds) to avoid calculation errors.
 
• **Force-Mass Relationship**: If multiple masses are combined and the same force is applied, the **acceleration will always decrease** compared to the acceleration of the individual masses because the total inertia of the system has increased.
 
• **Linear Relationship**: The relationship **F = ma** assumes that the mass remains constant during the motion, which is true for most **non-relativistic** macroscopic calculations.

questions.question: 4a2b is a four digit number divisible by 3. Select the correct possible values of a and b from the following.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be divisible by 3, the sum of its digits must be a multiple of 3.

Sum of digits of 4a2b = 4 + a + 2 + b = 6 + a + b.

Since 6 is a multiple of 3, the sum (a + b) must also be a multiple of 3.

Checking the options, only a = 0 and b = 0 gives a + b = 0, which is divisible by 3.

**∴ The correct answer is a = 0, b = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of digits = 4 + a + 2 + b = 6 + a + b

⇒ For 4a2b to be divisible by 3, (6 + a + b) must be a multiple of 3.

⇒ Since 6 is already a multiple of 3, the expression (a + b) must be a multiple of 3 (i.e., 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, etc.).

⇒ Let us evaluate the given options systematically:

⇒ Option 1: a = 0, b = 0 ⇒ a + b = 0 + 0 = 0 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ Option 2: a = 3, b = 1 ⇒ a + b = 3 + 1 = 4 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ Option 3: a = 2, b = 0 ⇒ a + b = 2 + 0 = 2 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ Option 4: a = 0, b = 1 ⇒ a + b = 0 + 1 = 1 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ Thus, the only possible valid values among the choices are a = 0 and b = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is a = 0, b = 0.**

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9.

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

A number is divisible by 6 if it is an even number (divisible by 2) and the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3 (divisible by 3).

questions.question: Due to water crisis, 38% of the initial population left the village, and 50% of the remaining left the village for pursuing jobs. If presently 1550 people inhabit the village, what is the ratio of the initial population to the present population?

Let the initial population be 100 units.

**∴ The correct answer is 100:31.**

This threshold reflects the average of the national poverty lines of the world’s poorest countries.

questions.question: Which of the following protected areas in Odisha is proposed to be upgraded to a National Park, thereby becoming the state’s third national park as of September 2025?

__
 
• The **Odisha Government** has formally moved a proposal to the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to upgrade the **Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary** to a **National Park**.

• Currently, **Odisha** has only two designated National Parks: **Similipal National Park** in **Mayurbhanj** and **Bhitarkanika National Park** in **Kendrapara**.
 
• The sanctuary is spread over an area of approximately **342.91 square kilometers** and is located in the **Sambalpur district**.
 
• The upgrade is intended to provide higher statutory protection to the habitat, which boasts one of the highest **herbivore densities** in the country and is a significant **Eco-Sensitive Zone**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Features**:
 
 
• **Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary** is situated on the **Barapahad hills** and serves as a crucial catchment area for the **Hirakud Dam**, which is one of the longest earthen dams in the world.
 
• The sanctuary is famous for its "dry deciduous forests" and its proximity to the **Mahanadi River**, making it a prime spot for **ecotourism**.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna**:
 
 
• It is home to a significant population of **Indian Gaur** (Bison), **Leopards**, and the **four-horned antelope** (**Chousingha**).
 
• The **Hirakud Reservoir** adjacent to the sanctuary attracts more than **1.5 lakh** migratory birds of nearly **50 species** during the **winter season**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance**:
 
 
• The sanctuary has historical links to the legendary freedom fighter **Veer Surendra Sai**, who utilized the dense forests of **Barapahad** as a base for his guerrilla warfare against the **British** during the **1857** uprising.

• **Legal Framework**:
 
 
• A **National Park** is established under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**. Unlike a sanctuary, no human activity or private land rights are permitted inside a National Park unless specifically authorized.
 
• The **State Government** has the power to declare an area a National Park by notification if it is considered to be of adequate ecological, faunal, or floral importance.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options**:
 
 
• **Bhitarkanika Wildlife Sanctuary**: Part of this sanctuary was declared a **National Park** in **1998**. It is a **Ramsar site** known for its **mangroves** and **saltwater crocodiles**.
 
• **Satkosia Gorge Wildlife Sanctuary**: Located in the **Angul district**, it was declared a **Tiger Reserve** in **2007**. It is famous for the **Gharial** conservation program in the **Mahanadi River**.
 
• **Sunabeda Wildlife Sanctuary**: Situated in the **Nuapada district**, it is known for the rare **wild buffalo** and has been proposed as a **Tiger Reserve** to expand the conservation area for big cats in the **central Indian landscape**.
 
 
</ul

__
 
• **The Order of St Michael and St George** is the premier honour awarded to **British nationals** and others for **outstanding service abroad or internationally**, particularly in relation to **Foreign and Commonwealth affairs**.
 
• It is traditionally featured in the **King’s Birthday Overseas & International Honours List**, which recognizes individuals serving the **United Kingdom**'s interests internationally or those performing exceptional **charitable or voluntary work** abroad.
 
• Founded in **1818** by the **Prince Regent** (later **King George IV**), the order was originally created to commemorate the **Ionian Islands** becoming a British protectorate and for service in **Malta**.
 
• The order consists of three ranks: **Knight or Dame Grand Cross (GCMG)**, **Knight or Dame Commander (KCMG or DCMG)**, and **Companion (CMG)**.
 
• In the context of the **2025** honours, this specific order is used to reward **diplomats**, **colonial officials**, and individuals involved in **international relations** and **global development**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Order of the British Empire**:
 
 
• Established by **King George V** in **1917**, this order recognizes a wide range of service to the **United Kingdom** across many sectors, including **arts, sciences, and public service**.
 
• It includes levels such as **GBE**, **KBE/DBE**, **CBE**, **OBE**, and **MBE**. While it can be awarded to people abroad, it is the standard order for **national achievement** within the **UK**.
 
 
 
• **The Royal Victorian Order**:
 
 
• Founded by **Queen Victoria** in **1896**, this is a **dynastic order** of knighthood.
 
• It is uniquely in the **personal gift of the Monarch** and is awarded for services rendered specifically to the **Sovereign** or members of the **Royal Family**, rather than on the advice of the **Prime Minister**.
 
 
 
• **The King’s Police Medal (KPM)**:
 
 
• This medal is awarded to members of the **police forces** in the **United Kingdom** and **Commonwealth** for **distinguished service** or **gallantry**.
 
• Following the accession of **King Charles III**, the award was renamed from the **Queen's Police Medal**.
 
 
 
• **Selection Process**:
 
 
• Honours in the **Overseas and International List** are recommended by the **Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO)**.
 
• The **2025 King's Birthday Honours** serve as one of two major annual lists (alongside the **New Year Honours**) that celebrate the contributions of individuals to **British society** and the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Motto and Symbolism**: The motto of **The Order of St Michael and St George** is **"Auspicium Melioris Aevi"**, which translates to **"Token of a better age"**.
 
• **The Chapel**: The primary chapel for this order is located within **St Paul's Cathedral** in **London**, which serves as a site for official ceremonies related to the order.

questions.question: The Sachet App provides real-time alerts about which type of emergencies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Natural disasters**__.

__
 
• The **Sachet App** is a mobile application developed and launched by the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** to provide citizens with real-time alerts and warnings specifically regarding **natural disasters**.
 
• The application serves as a unified platform under the **Integrated Alert System**, designed to disseminate critical information about impending **emergencies** such as **floods**, **cyclones**, **earthquakes**, **heatwaves**, and **landslides**.
 
• It utilizes a **geo-targeted** mechanism, meaning users receive alerts based on their specific **geographical location**, ensuring that only relevant and timely information reaches those in the danger zone.
 
• The app is built upon the **Common Alerting Protocol (CAP)**, a global standard for emergency messaging that ensures consistency across different communication channels like **SMS**, **Radio**, and **Television**.
 
• In addition to warnings, the app provides **"Do’s and Don’ts"** for various disaster scenarios, empowering citizens with actionable knowledge to ensure their safety during a **natural calamity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA):**
 
 
• It is the apex statutory body for disaster management in **India**, established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**.
 
• The **NDMA** is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India** and is responsible for laying down policies, plans, and guidelines for disaster management to ensure a timely and effective response.
 
 
 
• **Common Alerting Protocol (CAP):**
 
 
• **CAP** is a digital format for exchanging emergency alerts and public warnings over various networks.
 
• It was implemented in **India** through the **Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT)**, enabling a "one-stop" shop for all **alert-generating agencies**.
 
 
 
• **Technical Collaboration:**
 
 
• The alert system integrates data from various national agencies including the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** for weather, the **Central Water Commission (CWC)** for floods, and the **Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS)** for tsunamis.
 
• The **Sachet App** supports **multi-lingual** alerts, allowing users to receive information in several **regional Indian languages** to overcome linguistic barriers during **crises**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Phased Rollout:** The **CAP-compliant** integrated alert system was rolled out in phases across **India**, starting with high-risk coastal **states** to mitigate the impact of **cyclones**.
 
• **Zero Cost:** The **Sachet App** is a free-to-use government service, aimed at reaching the maximum number of citizens, including those in **rural** and **remote areas**.
 
• **Disaster Resilience:** This initiative is a part of **India's** broader commitment to the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030)**, which emphasizes the use of **technology** and early warning systems to save lives.
</ul
